answer.evidence: The lamppost is a 2px-wide pole (rows 12-46) with a thin bent arm curving over at rows 8-11 and a lantern hanging at rows 12-19 (width 7). The pole is a single flat-colored vertical strip, the same width at the top as lower down (width 2 at rows 20-29 and 32-44). The top end has no elliptical cap plate overhanging the shaft; the widest top row is only the lantern (7 wide) and it is drawn as a face-on rectangle with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The base at rows 45-46 is a tiny 4px foot with no ellipse. There is no top surface anywhere, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference is prop-lamp-crook. The candidate is a thin pole with a small green lantern at the bent top. Per-tile tone counts are 0 for both because the objects are thin, so I judged density by eye. The candidate has 10 distinct colours against the reference's 14. The pole reads as a nearly uniform dark line with little highlight or ramp, and the base is weak or missing. The reference has a visible base, a pole with a highlight edge, a curved hook and a glowing lantern with several tones. The candidate's dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, but so are the reference's, so that fact does not separate them. The candidate looks thinner, flatter and more sticker-like than the reference. When in doubt, fail.
